name: artifact_list
description: The artifact templates you can make with no network (slalom, hoop_course, repo_activity, cell, heart, brain, plant_cell, eye, dna, double_pendulum, solar_system), the data sources an artifact can read here (with their columns, and whether only sample data is on this headset), the artifacts already on this headset, and which one is open.

name: artifact_create
description:
Make an artifact and open it, for ANY request to make, build, show or simulate something; never say you can't first. Say in under 8 words what you're building, then call it. Templates (offline; inputs change their numbers): slalom (truck course), hoop_course (drone hoops), repo_activity (what shipped), cell, heart, brain, plant_cell, eye, dna (biology: always the template, never your own parts or facts), double_pendulum (chaos), solar_system (orbits). Courses are laid out on the real floor by the headset: never give room positions. Otherwise write manifest and scene yourself.
WRITING ONE. Metres, degrees, seconds. Y is up. The person looks along +z (nearer is smaller z; a negative z rotation turns clockwise). Build it 0.2 to 0.6 m across, centred on 0,0,0, at real proportions, each part touching what holds it up.
manifest: {"title":..,"inputs":[{"name":"speed","type":"number","min":0,"max":4,"default":1,"label":"Speed"}]}. Input types: number or integer (a choice is an integer 0..N-1). The tool fills every other manifest field and lists them in 'filled'.
scene: {"space":"volume","view":{"radius":R},"nodes":[..],"rules":[..]}, R about half its size; panel space only for controls with no 3D parts; never room.
nodes: one flat list. Each: id (a-z, 0-9, _), kind, optional parent (id), pos, rot, scale ([x,y,z], local to the parent), visible. Use exactly these field names (position, rotation, children, scripts, onClick are refused).
- primitive: shape box|sphere|cylinder|capsule|cone|plane, size [x,y,z] (full size; a cylinder stands along y), color "#RRGGBB", glow true for a light. No group kind: parts that move together are children of one primitive (hub, beam, pivot); a child's pos is from its centre.
- text: text, height (0.02 to 0.03), color, billboard; "{name}" shows a live metric.
- line: points [[x,y,z],..] or through [ids with the same parent], width, color.
- panel: title, widgets, pos. All controls live here: note{text}, slider{input}, button{id,label}, stat{metric,label,unit,decimals}.
- timeline: duration_s, loop, autoplay (default false). Nothing else.
- sim: solver pendulum or n_body, bodies, params, rate. Pendulum body: {node,length,angle,omega,mass}, angle 0 straight down, in the sim's x-y plane; bodies are its children.
HOW IT ACTS (nothing else runs; no scripts):
1 Slider: write "$name" for a number in pos, rot, scale, size, line points or width, text height, sim params or rate; it follows live: "rot":[0,0,"$tilt"].
2 Button: {"type":"button","id":"go","label":"Go"} needs a rule {"type":"on_input","input":"go","do":[..]}. Each action has one verb: {"timeline":id,"action":"play|pause|restart"}, {"sim":id,"action":"play|pause|restart"} or {"set":"<node>.visible","value":true|false}. States: one node per look, one button per state showing it and hiding the rest.
3 Motion: a timeline plus {"type":"animate","target":id,"property":"pos|rot|scale|color|visible","timeline":id,"keys":[[t,value],..]}. Keys are plain values, linear. A turn every T s: loop true, rot keys [[0,[0,0,0]],[T,[0,0,-360]]]. Animate each node property once. Without autoplay true, a button must play it.
4 Turning at a speed a slider sets: a sim pendulum with params {"g":0}, a body with omega in degrees per second, and "rate":"$speed". Draw the arm as a line through [a centre child, the body]. Swings, falls and orbits are sims, not keys.
5 Live numbers: {"type":"metric","name":"t","op":"sim","sim":id,"value":"time|flips|angle_1"}, shown by a stat or "{t}".
EXAMPLE {"manifest":{"title":"Stopwatch"},"scene":{"space":"volume","view":{"radius":0.25},"nodes":[{"id":"dial","kind":"primitive","shape":"cylinder","size":[0.36,0.01,0.36],"pos":[0,0,0.01],"rot":[90,0,0],"color":"#161B26"},{"id":"pivot","kind":"primitive","shape":"sphere","size":[0.02,0.02,0.02],"pos":[0,0,-0.01]},{"id":"hand","kind":"primitive","parent":"pivot","shape":"box","size":[0.006,0.15,0.004],"pos":[0,0.065,0],"color":"#FF8A3D"},{"id":"clock","kind":"timeline","duration_s":60,"loop":true},{"id":"ui","kind":"panel","title":"Stopwatch","widgets":[{"type":"button","id":"start","label":"Start"},{"type":"button","id":"stop","label":"Stop"}]}],"rules":[{"type":"animate","target":"pivot","property":"rot","timeline":"clock","keys":[[0,[0,0,0]],[60,[0,0,-360]]]},{"type":"on_input","input":"start","do":[{"timeline":"clock","action":"play"}]},{"type":"on_input","input":"stop","do":[{"timeline":"clock","action":"pause"}]}]}}
RESULTS. 'invalid': nothing saved; fix every error (see each hint) and resend the whole manifest and scene now; if next says stop, stop and tell the person. 'built': tell them what to press or drag. 'say': tell them in your own words. awaiting_approval: ask them to tap Allow. no_free_floor, no_headroom, no_room_data, no_data: pass them on. Data: a source from artifact_list in manifest.data, read by an array node with source {table, grid}; never type rows in.

inputs.description: Optional starting values for a template. Slalom: {"gates": 6, "spacing_m": 1.0}, gates 3 to 12, spacing 0.6 to 2.0 m. Hoop course: {"hoops": 5, "spacing_m": 1.2}, hoops 3 to 10, spacing 0.6 to 2.0 m.

manifest.description: Instead of a template: the manifest. title is enough; the tool fills the rest.

scene.description: Instead of a template: the scene.

name: artifact_open
description: Open an artifact that's on this headset by id. A course reuses its saved layout in this room, so runs compare fairly.

name: artifact_relayout
description: Lay the open course out again in this room, for when furniture moved or the person wants it somewhere else. The old layout and its runs are kept, but new runs won't compare like for like with old ones.

name: artifact_run
description: Arm a scored run on the open artifact (or open it first). The Thing entering the start zone starts the timer; finishing through every gate or hoop, crashing or rolling over, missing one, or timing out writes a run record and attaches it to the notebook.

name: artifact_compare
description: Put run metrics side by side. If runs isn't given, the two newest. Runs on a different course are labelled; never treat those as a clean comparison.
